entry.source: וַיְקַו לְמִשְׁפָּט וְהִנֵּה מִשְׂפָּח לִצְדָקָה וְהִנֵּה צְעָקָה
entry.translit: wayqaw lᵉmišpāṭ wᵉhinnēh miśpāḥ, liṣḏāqāh wᵉhinnēh ṣᵉʿāqāh
entry.literal: he waited for justice, and behold, [miśpāḥ]; for righteousness, and behold, a cry
entry.standardEnglish: he looked for justice, but, behold, oppression; for righteousness, but, behold, a cry (ASV)
entry.wohChoice: 'he waited for justice, but behold, bloodshed; for righteousness, but behold, an outcry' — miśpāḥ 'bloodshed' (BDB; NRSV); ṣᵉʿāqāh 'an outcry' under the central zaaqah-outcry-of-the-oppressed entry. Presentation rule: the paronomasia (mišpāṭ/miśpāḥ, ṣᵉḏāqāh/ṣᵉʿāqāh) is NOT reproduced in the line, either by parenthetical transliteration or by a sound-echo; it is explained in commentary.
entry.rationale: מִשְׂפָּח occurs only here, and its meaning has to be recovered from etymology and from the pun. BDB places it under a root 'pour out' (cf. Arabic safaḥa 'shed blood') with the sense 'outpouring (of blood), bloodshed', the value NRSV adopts; ASV 'oppression' and JPS 1917 'violence' give the general sense the context requires without a lexical basis. The Editor adopts 'bloodshed' because it has the etymological support, it matches the forensic cry of victims in the parallel ṣᵉʿāqāh (the blood that 'cries out', ṣōʿăqîm, Gen 4:10), and it echoes the hands 'full of blood' of Isa 1:15; because the derivation is not certain, the claim is inferred rather than direct. On presentation: the Translator's draft placed the four transliterations in parentheses in the line, which has almost no precedent in the corpus and turns the verse into an apparatus. Sound-echoes such as NJPS 'justice … injustice; equity … iniquity' keep the pun but change the meaning of both second terms, which accuracy-before-lens rules out. The line therefore carries the plain meanings and the commentary on 5:7 states the pun with the Hebrew forms (Wildberger, Isaiah 1-12, 1991; Williamson, ICC Isaiah 1-5, 2006). The split pair mišpāṭ/ṣᵉḏāqāh is rendered 'justice'/'righteousness' but is not placed under the central tzedakah-u-mishpat-justice-pair entry, following the 32:16 split-pair precedent of wave I2.

entry.partOfSpeech: verb + noun (nep̄eš in its physical sense)
entry.literal: She'ol has made wide its throat
entry.wohChoice: 'She'ol has widened its throat' — nep̄eš in its physical sense 'throat, gullet', parallel to pîhā 'its mouth'.
entry.rationale: נֶפֶשׁ has 'throat, gullet' as a basic physical sense alongside 'appetite, life, self' (HALOT nepeš 1; cf. Ps 69:2; Jonah 2:6), and the parallel colon 'and opened its mouth beyond measure' fixes that sense here. NJPS renders 'gullet' and the same idiom of a widened nep̄eš describes insatiable greed at Hab 2:5 ('who widens his nep̄eš like She'ol'). ASV 'enlarged her desire' abstracts the image into appetite and loses the anatomical parallelism the verse builds. The Editor therefore renders 'widened its throat'; the sense is lexicon-attested and adopted by a major modern version, so the claim is direct. The central nefesh-blessing-transfer entry (Gen 27, nep̄eš as agent of blessing, transliterated) has a different register and is deliberately not applied; the Ugaritic parallel of Mot's devouring jaws (KTU 1.5 II 2-4) is noted in commentary only.

entry.strongs: H1197 (bʿr; Strong's does not separate the homonyms)
entry.partOfSpeech: verb, Piel infinitive construct with lᵉ
entry.literal: and it shall be for grazing / for being browsed
entry.standardEnglish: it shall be eaten up (ASV); it shall be devoured (NRSV)
entry.wohChoice: 'it shall be eaten up' (ASV) — bʿr II 'graze, browse', paired with lᵉmirmās 'for trampling'. The 6:13 entry levaer-massevet-stump-isaiah (bʿr I 'for burning') does not govern this site.
entry.rationale: The same form לְבָעֵר is rendered 'for burning' at 6:13 under levaer-massevet-stump-isaiah, whose rationale records 'be browsed' as a minority construal there. In 5:5 the context decides the other way: the hedge is removed so that the vineyard is opened to animals, and the parallel colon has lᵉmirmās 'for trampling', which points to the homonym bʿr II 'graze, browse' (HALOT; cf. the Hiphil of livestock grazing a field, Exod 22:4). ASV 'eaten up', NRSV 'devoured' and the standard commentaries read it so (Wildberger, Isaiah 1-12; Williamson, ICC Isaiah 1-5). A separate entry is made, rather than a context clause in the 6:13 entry, because the lexicons treat the two as distinct roots, and recording the split keeps the two renderings of one written form auditable. The rendering is the standard one and carries no lens.

entry.source: בְּכָל־זֹאת לֹא־שָׁב אַפּוֹ וְעוֹד יָדוֹ נְטוּיָה
entry.translit: bᵉḵol-zōʾṯ lōʾ-šāḇ ʾappô wᵉʿôḏ yāḏô nᵉṭûyāh
entry.partOfSpeech: refrain (verbal clause + nominal clause with passive participle)
entry.literal: in all this his nose/anger has not turned, and still his hand is stretched out
entry.standardEnglish: For all this his anger is not turned away, but his hand is stretched out still (ASV)
entry.wohChoice: 'For all this his anger has not turned away, and his hand is stretched out still' — fixed wording for every occurrence of the refrain (5:25; Heb. 9:11, 16, 20; 10:4).
entry.rationale: The refrain closes 5:25 and each strophe of the poem of 9:7-10:4 (Heb. 9:11, 16, 20; 10:4; Eng. 9:12, 17, 21; 10:4), and many commentators hold that 5:25-30 belongs with that poem (Wildberger, Isaiah 1-12; Blenkinsopp, Isaiah 1-39, AB 19, 2000; Williamson). One fixed English wording is needed so that the repetition stays visible across chapters. šûḇ with ʾap as subject is the idiom for anger subsiding (Gen 27:44-45; Hos 14:5), for which English 'turn away' is the established equivalent (ASV, NRSV); the Translator's 'turned back' is literal but not idiomatic. lōʾ-šāḇ is rendered as a perfect, 'has not turned away', because the strokes the poem lists have already fallen, and the waw of wᵉʿôḏ is rendered 'and' rather than ASV's interpretive 'but'. The rendering is standard and carries no lens. Forward scope: when chapters 9-10 are drafted, ISA-9:11, ISA-9:16, ISA-9:20 and ISA-10:4 (Hebrew versification, the corpus refId basis) should be added to appliesTo and rendered identically.

note: Standard title at its first occurrences in the book's opening section; no change to wohChoice.
5:16 hāʾēl haqqāḏôš 'God the Holy One' — ʾēl designating YHWH; 'God' per the entry.
5:24 tôraṯ YHWH ṣᵉḇāʾôṯ 'the teaching of YHWH of hosts', parallel to ʾimrāh 'word' (as 1:10).

changes.wohChoice: 'the earth' — hā-ʾāreṣ rendered in its cosmic-universal scope wherever Isaiah speaks of the whole world: the world-judgment register of chapter 24, the universal judgment of 13:9-13, the creation and universal contexts of chs. 40-65, and the universal-horizon idiom qᵉṣēh hāʾāreṣ 'the end(s) of the earth' (5:26; 40:28). The Genesis-1 corpus rendering ʾereṣ='land' (local/durational) is deliberately NOT applied at these sites; territorial ʾereṣ elsewhere in Isaiah stays 'land' under the central eretz entry. ʿiwwāh p̄ānehā 'twists its surface' (24:1, over ASV 'turneth it upside down').

note: 5:26 miqqᵉṣēh hāʾāreṣ 'from the end of the earth', the universal horizon idiom, as the entry was already applied at 40:28 'the ends of the earth'. 5:8 and 5:30 stay 'land' under the central eretz entry (territorial). Recommend the orchestrator note in the wohChoice wording that the entry now governs universal-horizon idioms book-wide (its text still says 'throughout chapter 24').
